relations.subject: Heinrich Kiepert
relations.evidence: His family was friends with Leopold von Ranke, who inspired Kiepert's creative endeavors.

relations.subject: Heinrich Kiepert
relations.evidence: Kiepert was taught by August Meineke in school. Meineke influenced Kiepert's interest in classical antiquity.

relations.subject: Heinrich Kiepert
relations.evidence: He attended Humboldt University of Berlin. He studied history, philology, and geography.

relations.subject: Heinrich Kiepert
relations.evidence: He published his first geographical work, with Carl Ritter, in 1840, titled Atlas von Hellas und den hellenischen Kolonien.

relations.subject: Heinrich Kiepert
relations.evidence: Kiepert taught geography at the University of Humboldt-Berlin starting in 1854. He taught at the university until his death.

relations.subject: Richard Kiepert
relations.evidence: His son, cartographer Richard Kiepert published remaining works by Kiepert after his death
